---
title: "Practice data"
subtitle: "A small, honest starter pack so you can actually run the commands."
toc: true
---

The fastest way to learn is to run things yourself. This page gives you a tiny
starter pack: a study-design template, a few synthetic reads for instant format
practice, and a reproducible script that fetches a real reference genome. Nothing
here is large, and nothing pretends to be something it is not.

## How to use it

::: {.cba-modsteps}
1. **Make a project folder** &nbsp;·&nbsp; keep everything for one analysis together
2. **Add the metadata** &nbsp;·&nbsp; copy `metadata_template.csv` and fill in your samples
3. **Get the reads** &nbsp;·&nbsp; start with the toy reads, or run `get_reference.sh` for a real genome
4. **Run the module** &nbsp;·&nbsp; follow the matching lesson and compare against its expected output
:::

Put the files in one folder and run the fetch script from a terminal where Conda
is active (see [Module 01](modules/01-setup-environment/)):

```bash
mkdir practice-project && cd practice-project
# copy the downloaded files into this folder, then:
bash get_reference.sh
ls
```

```
# expected (yours may differ)
get_reference.sh   metadata_template.csv   sars2.fasta   toy_reads_R1.fastq   toy_reads_R2.fastq
```

## Expected outputs

You do not have to guess whether a command worked. Every module shows the output
you should expect to see after each key step, so you can compare line by line. If
your result does not match, that mismatch is the lesson: go back and find out why.

::: {.callout-important collapse="true"}
## A note on honesty (please read)
- The **toy reads are synthetic**. They are made-up sequences for format practice,
  not real biological data. Never report results from them as if they meant
  something.
- Real datasets are kept **out of the repository on purpose**. The honest,
  reproducible way to share data is a small script that fetches it (like
  `get_reference.sh`), so anyone can recreate the exact inputs.
- The **single-cell and spatial modules use their own datasets** suited to those
  methods. They are not automatic downstream products of one bulk RNA-seq run.
- Accessions, URLs, and tool behaviour change over time. When something does not
  match, trust the official documentation over this page.
:::
